Subject: Request: brief walk-through of sandbox proxy + isolation model for Dedicated/Private

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. The Veridian security team is assembling a tight evidence bundle for our procurement review and we have a few clarifying asks about how Redwood approaches tenant encapsulation for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically: 

- Can you provide a short network walk-through showing the sandbox/proxy pattern you mentioned (management vs. data plane separation)?
- How does egress filtering operate for customer VPCs on Private? Is there an enforced proxy/bastion or do you rely on routing/ACLs?
- Any concise diagram or sequence that shows automatic fallback when a preferred model pool is unavailable (i.e., routing to a compatible variant) would help our risk assessment.

If you can share a diagram and a 1-page narrative we can include in the SIG and CAIQ responses. Ideally by Monday (23rd) so we can keep our procurement timeline.

Cheers,
James Lowe
Security Engineer, Veridian Systems
security@veridian.com

P.S. Happy to sign an NDA if that helps with any internal screenshots or configuration snippets you prefer not to publish.

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: brief walk-through of sandbox proxy + isolation model for Dedicated/Private

Hi James — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the diagram and a short packet that maps the items to typical SIG/CAIQ control questions. High level points below, and I cc'd Kim and Lauren to add any operational/edge detail: 

- Architecture summary (attached: redwood_mesh_diagram_v3.png): For Dedicated and Private we enforce a multi-layered boundary: (1) tenant overlay (namespace-level isolation) inside the runtime, (2) enforced egress via regional outbound proxies for Private deployments, and (3) control plane endpoints that are logically and network-wise reachable only from management subnets (private peering / VPC endpoints).
- Proxy vs routing: Private deployments default to a forced-proxy model for outbound traffic from inference hosts — this gives us a single choke point for egress filtering, DLP integrations, and customer-supplied IP allowlists. Dedicated (Redwood-managed) deployments may use an integrated outbound NAT/proxy depending on the customer's network posture; we document both patterns in the attached PDF.
- Fallback/routing behavior (attached: proxy-fallback-flow.pdf): Requests are policy-routed by tenant and model version. If a primary pool is saturated or degraded, the smart router evaluates candidate variants (latency/cost/compatibility) and routes to the next best pool. KV cache prefixes and request affinities guide safe reroutes to avoid cross-tenant contamination.

Can you confirm if Veridian needs network-level traces or just the architecture artifacts for SIG/CAIQ? If traces are required we can coordinate with your security team and exchange an NDA scope to redact customer-specific addresses.

Regards,

Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 09:24 AM chloe.martin@redwood.ai wrote:
> Can you confirm if Veridian needs network-level traces or just the architecture artifacts for SIG/CAIQ?

James — quick operational notes to accompany Chloe's packet: 

- Management/control plane: We maintain separate VPC peering (or private endpoints in customer VPCs for Private installs) such that the control plane endpoints are only accessible from documented management subnets. There are explicit security groups and flow logs enabled; we provide a checklist (attached: controlplane-segmentation-checklist.xlsx) that maps the controls to SIG/CAT questions.
- Egress enforcement: For Private we install an outbound proxy in each region that terminates TLS and performs allowlist/DLP hooks as configured by the customer. We provide both an inline proxy option and a transparent proxy mode; the inline mode is enforced when regulatory constraints require content inspection.
- Tenant fencing: Runtime namespaces and token scoping ensure KV cache isolation. We also scrub logs at collection time and route observability data through a sanitized telemetry pipeline.

Lauren — can you drop a one-line confirmation of the operational SLA we offer for Dedicated fallback routing (99.5% routing availability) so James can include it in his procurement note?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

- Can you confirm whether the proxy logs include full request URIs by default or if that is optionally enabled? (We have to assess potential PII leakage.)
- For the fallback routing, is there an explicit TTL or affinity window used to prevent immediate cross-pool sticky failures?

If you can reply with those two bullets we should be able to bundle this into our CAIQ and mark the control as 'mapped'. We don't need packet captures — the higher-level artifacts are sufficient.
